$comment: Reviewed thresholds for the admission gauntlet. These are DATA, not code:
changing one changes what the system will accept, so a change here is a
reviewed PR like any other. Values marked null are unset until Phase 1
records real baselines on real data — a guessed threshold that never
fires is worse than an absent one, because it reads as protection.
G1. Rolling sources whose pinned bytes have no durable archive yet.
This list is an ACKNOWLEDGEMENT, not a permission slip. A source named
here is one we know is unarchived and have accepted the risk on, dated
and reviewed. A rolling source NOT named here fails the build closed, so
the gap can never grow silently — which is the guardrail. Emptying this
list is the goal; adding to it is a reviewed decision.
Why acknowledge rather than warn: a warning that appears on every PR,
that its author cannot clear, and that is unrelated to their change,
becomes decoration by exactly the mechanism CLAUDE.md's gate discipline
forbids — and it would make the documented merge criterion (verdict
ADMIT) permanently unreachable.
2026-08-08: openbible-topics and openbible-xrefs. a.openbible.info rolls
its files weekly with no upstream archive, so our checksummed copies are
the only ones in existence. Closing this needs a Release upload, which no
build script can perform — see docs/NEEDS-JESSE.md §1.8.

size.$comment_total: 160 MiB. Base scripture corpus is ~122 MiB; Layers A+B are budgeted ~30 MiB with headroom.
$comment_perTable: Per-table byte budgets, INCLUDING each table's indexes — an index ships with
its table and grows with it, so budgeting the table alone would miss two
thirds of what verse_terms actually costs.
Set 2026-07-30 from the first measured artifact (117.60 MiB total), with
headroom sized to intent rather than uniformly: verse_terms is the table that
grows when a commentator is admitted, so it gets room for roughly one more
whole-Bible author; the corpus tables are fixed by the translation and get
little. These are FIRST REAL VALUES and want Jesse's review — before today
these budgets named tables that did not exist and no gate read them.

FTS shadow tables are budgeted too: they are part of what ships, they grow with the corpus, and the gate reports any unbudgeted table over 1 MiB rather than passing it silently — which is how verses_fts_data was found.

$comment: p95 over the probe set, measured AFTER a warm-up pass, on whatever CI
runner GitHub provides. Deliberately loose relative to observed local
times (~5ms): a shared runner varies by several-fold, and a gate that
fails at random teaches people to ignore gates. What this catches is an
ALGORITHMIC regression - an accidental full scan, a dropped index - which
shows up as an order of magnitude, not a few milliseconds.
Target-hardware latency is a consumer's measurement, not this repo's.

collision.$comment: G4. Two concepts whose lexicons overlap beyond these thresholds are near-duplicates and must be merged or differentiated.

distinctiveness.$comment: G5. Terms below the PMI floor never enter a verse profile, so generic vocabulary cannot accumulate into evidence. The cap is PER VERSE since Layer B resolved to verse keys.

$comment: G6 reviewed-constants mirror of the engine's ranking constants
(engine/src/ranking/budgets.ts). Built INCREMENTALLY by the 0.10.0
stages - each stage adds the constant it introduces - and complete at
squash time. reviewedConstantsCheck fails on any key here that does not
equal the engine's value, and on any key the engine does not export, so
a constant cannot be retuned in code without this reviewed-data change
travelling in the same commit. Changing a value here changes ordering:
ENGINE_VERSION must bump in the same commit (covenant #2).
soleEvidenceMaxPoints (stage 1, P3.1): a result whose EVERY surviving
reason family is named in this map has its total capped at the named
ceiling - in practice a lone translation_variant caps at 6, below
token_overlap's 10 and level with proximity/cross_reference, so a
bag-of-stems vocabulary hint can accompany but never overrule an honest
text match. The value 6 is plan-recommended pending J20 sign-off, which
rides the normal approval flow.
exactPhraseFullAuthorityWords (stage 3, P3.3): the significant-word
count at which a verbatim phrase earns FULL exact_phrase authority.
Below 2 significant words a verbatim occurrence files as token_overlap
at 10 points; 2 words earn 2/3 authority (40 points, level with the
concept_anchor ceiling and above weakAggregateCap 30); 3+ earn the full
60. FIXED, not a tuning knob: raising it to 4 would push 2-word phrases
to 30, colliding with weakAggregateCap and endangering correct
remembered-phrase verbatim #1s. The value 3 is plan-recommended pending
J19 sign-off, which rides the normal approval flow.
passageTermPmiHalfSaturation (stage 5, P3.5): half-saturation constant
of the asymptotic passage_terms PMI factor
pmiSum / (pmiSum + matchedTerms x this). A match whose mean per-term
PMI equals this value scores factor 0.5; the G5 admission floor
(distinctiveness.minPmi 2.0, above) scores 0.25; the measured corpus
mean 6.37 scores ~0.52. Asymptotic, not min()-capped: distinctive
vocabulary lives above any per-term cap (measured corpus PMI range
2.02-18.54), so a capped form leaves the flat ties it exists to break
byte-identical. Strictly monotone - distinct pmiSums never tie. The
value 6.0 is plan-recommended pending J21 sign-off, which rides the
normal approval flow.
chipDisplayMinPoints (P3.7, CO-2/F22): chips display points at one
decimal; a chip below this value prints '0.0', asserting a
contribution the display itself denies, so it is withheld
(display-only - the points still count, ordering untouched; a result
always keeps at least its strongest chip). Fixed by display
precision (the smallest value that rounds to 0.1), not a tuning
knob. Measured at introduction: no chip anywhere in the 84-query
battery's full 25-deep windows is below it - a structural guard on
the display contract.
passageTermChipDisplayFloor (P3.7, CO-2/F22): passage_terms chips
below this many points are withheld (display-only, same semantics
as above). Derived from reviewed data, not tuned: the weakest
evidence G5 can admit - one term at distinctiveness.minPmi 2.0 on a
one-verse note - earns 8 x log1p(1)/log1p(6) x 2/(2+6) ~ 0.712
points, and the floor sits just beneath it, so undiluted
admission-floor evidence still displays while the same evidence
diluted by span or aggregate caps is withheld. Measured at
introduction: the weakest passage_terms chip in the battery's full
windows is 0.896 - nothing currently withheld; the floor exists so
future admitted data cannot decorate results with
sub-admission-grade chips.

noise.$comment: G8. Measured against the previous artifact. Exceeding any of these fails the build and names the offending probes.
$comment_minMeanDistinctiveness: Deleted 2026-08-17 (eval-toughening PR-B). The key sat here as null and
no gate ever read it, so it read as protection while providing none -
worse than a missing threshold, because a reviewer scanning this file
would count it as coverage. If a mean-distinctiveness floor is ever
wanted, it returns together with a gate that reads it and a real
measured baseline, in one reviewed PR.
$comment_weak: Weak-reason share is gated as an INCREASE over baseline, not an absolute
ceiling. An absolute cap is meaningless while a query has no authoritative
signal available to it: a one-word thematic query like 'love' is 100% weak
in Phase 1 by construction, because concept anchors do not exist yet.
What we actually fear is the share CLIMBING as data accumulates - that is
precision erosion. So the delta is the gate and the absolute is recorded.

$comment: G12 rank-quality thresholds, in MICRO units (value × 10^6), integers
only — the gate compares exact rationals by integer cross-multiplication,
so a float here would claim a precision the arithmetic does not use.
Every quality threshold is NULL at introduction. Null means MEASURED AND
REPORTED: the Admission Report prints the value with '(no threshold —
baseline not yet established)' — never pass, never fail. A null flips to
a value only via the four-step protocol in
docs/governance/probe-baseline-review.md §Rank-metrics baselines:
≥3 ADMIT runs → --update-rank-baseline writes the candidate baseline
(machine never writes approvals) → an independent reviewer hand-authors
eval/baselines/rank-metrics.approval.json → the same PR flips the chosen
nulls quoting the run history. The gauntlet enforces that ordering
structurally: a non-null threshold here with no independently approved
rank-metrics baseline fails G12. Rollback of a flipped threshold is
null-with-tombstone (the noise.$comment_minMeanDistinctiveness pattern).

$comment_categoryFloors: Structural minimums, not quality thresholds: the nine seed counts of
the transcribed 84-query battery — known facts about the committed
specimen set, so they are non-null from day one (J44). An active-query
count below any floor is a G12 FAIL naming the category: the battery
has been hollowed out. Raising a floor as the battery grows is a
reviewed data change like any other threshold in this file.

$comment: E6: the measurable A-tier / S-tier definitions the tier report computes
(eval/src/tierReport.ts; npm run tier-report --workspace eval). Reviewed
data like every threshold in this file. The two percentage bars are
PROPOSED at the audit's suggested 90% / 98% and await Jesse's
ratification as HIS quality bar, not the audit's suggestion (J41);
the tier report is the mega-sweep phase's exit bar (sweep exits at
A-tier MET on the release artifact; S-tier is the standing target).
Tier semantics: a criterion prints MET / NOT MET / NOT EVALUABLE
(reason) / DISABLED. NOT EVALUABLE never satisfies a criterion - the
not-applicable-never-counts-as-pass rule applied to tiers. DISABLED is
different in kind: an explicit, dated editorial decision recorded here
removed the criterion, so it does not block. The two must never be
conflated - one is a measurement gap, the other is a decision.
Micro units (rate x 10^6), integers, compared by exact cross-
multiplication over battery-scoreable queries only (golden-derived
pins are fixture assertions, not the battery's graded set).

saturation.$comment: G9. A work that moves an already-covered pericope's profile less than minProfileDelta is recorded as saturated and skipped.

$comment: Gap-mining thresholds (docs/telemetry-and-gap-mining.md). Reviewed data
like everything else here. minDistinctDevices: a query string appears in
a Gap Report only when attested by at least this many distinct audit
tokens - below it, counted in aggregate, never printed. No major engine
publishes its own suppression threshold, so 3 is OUR chosen floor, not
an industry constant, and at congregation scale it is necessary but not
sufficient (the category exclusion list is the other half).
rawRetentionDays: on-device event lifetime, enforced by the shim.
weakConvertedRank: a cluster whose best converted rank is deeper than
this is verdict WEAK - we matched, but ranked it poorly.
